# 1.2.38 - the map takes clicks, the colour fades, the tile is constant

Ten things from the table, in the order they were reported.

**The map under the glass.** Nothing of the curtain may take a click, and the
sheet now says so with `!important` (the curtain, its layers, the glow, the
notice stack); the pinned right column takes none itself, the strip and the
tray opt back in. If the map still ignores the mouse somewhere, `drpgGlassDebug()`
in the console - and the report line in the Look window - now name the element
the pointer hits at the centre of the map. Send me that line.

**The Despair rail** is as wide as its rows, whatever the base sheet's cap.

**Notices have one piece of glass.** The bottom-left tile is 330 x 160 (scaled
with the screen), never measured and never recut: two short cards or one long
one, the newest at the bottom; a third card retires the oldest. A card arriving
or leaving no longer touches the curtain.

**The Look window** is 560 wide with a wider label column.

**The state colour fades.** The accent is a registered custom property now, so
it interpolates: every element under the theme fades its inherited value over
the turn (840 ms), and every plate, edge and `color-mix` follows frame by
frame. The curtain is excluded on purpose: it paints its canvas from the target
colour and its morph's ghost is its fade. A window's band repaints once the
fade has ended, behind its own Bone flash.

**Window controls have their icons back.** Foundry draws the close and collapse
buttons in their `::before`, where the brush also lives at opacity 0 - so the
icons were painted over with nothing. The controls are not brushes, and they
are Bone Dim on the band instead of the base sheet's Ink.

**Windows are the size of their content.** Module dialogs take the height of
what is in them, to the screen; anything taller scrolls inside the window
instead of being cut.

**The Event panel at a murder.** It showed nothing for the whole opening stage
(from "a murder begins" to the first incident roll), which on the GM's screen
read as "no panel". An opening card for the GM and the participants fills that
stage. And the panel sits under the Despair rail, not above it: it had no flex
order, and Foundry's column put an unnumbered item first.

**The objection cut** holds white on every seam for a fifth of 700 ms and
fades over the rest, instead of blinking for 90.

**The curtain stands still.** The drift watch compared rounded rectangles as
strings, so a counter ticking over, a roll card widening the status strip by a
pixel, a notice sliding in - each was a recut and a morph in the middle of
play. A block now has to move or grow by more than 4 px, twice in a row, and
the fixed tiles are not measured at all.
